title: Related rates
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:40Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point teaches average rate of change as a secant gradient, while the new point teaches related rates through the chain rule, which is a different idea.

draft.title: Related rates
card: A related rates problem links two quantities that both change with time t. The chain rule connects their rates: dV/dt = dV/dr × dr/dt.
Step 1: write an equation that links the quantities. Step 2: differentiate both sides with respect to t. Step 3: substitute the known values and solve.
Example: a sphere has V = 4/3 πr³, so dV/dt = 4πr² × dr/dt. If r = 2 cm and dr/dt = 0.5 cm/s, then dV/dt = 4π × 4 × 0.5 = 8π cm³/s.
Put in the numbers only after differentiating. A quantity that changes with time must not be replaced by its value before this step.
draft.remember: Write the link, differentiate with respect to t, then substitute the numbers.

a.q: A circular oil spill has area A = πr². Its radius grows at 3 m/min. What is dA/dt when r = 10 m?
a.why: dA/dt = 2πr × dr/dt = 2π × 10 × 3 = 60π m²/min. The option 30π comes from forgetting the 2 in 2πr.
a.clue: Differentiate A = πr² with respect to t first.

b.q: Air fills a spherical balloon at 36π cm³/s. Using V = 4/3 πr³, how fast is the radius growing when r = 3 cm?
b.why: dV/dt = 4πr² × dr/dt, so 36π = 4π × 9 × dr/dt = 36π × dr/dt. Then dr/dt = 1 cm/s. The option 3 comes from dividing by 12π, which is wrong.
b.clue: Find dV/dt in terms of dr/dt, then substitute r = 3.

final.title: Related rates
card: A related rates problem links two quantities that both change with time \(t\). The chain rule connects their rates: \(\frac{dV}{dt} = \frac{dV}{dr} \times \frac{dr}{dt}\).
Step 1: write an equation that links the quantities. Step 2: differentiate both sides with respect to \(t\). Step 3: substitute the known values and solve.

Example: a sphere has \(V = \frac{4}{3} \pi r^{3}\), so \(\frac{dV}{dt} = 4\pi r^{2} \times \frac{dr}{dt}\). If \(r = 2\) cm and \(\frac{dr}{dt} = 0.5\) cm/s, then \(\frac{dV}{dt} = 4\pi \times 4 \times 0.5 = 8\pi \text{ cm}^{3}/\text{s}\).
Put in the numbers only after differentiating. A quantity that changes with time must not be replaced by its value before this step.
final.remember: Write the link, differentiate with respect to \(t\), then substitute the numbers.

a.q: A circular oil spill has area \(A = \pi r^{2}\). Its radius grows at 3 m/min. What is \(\frac{dA}{dt}\) when \(r = 10\) m?
a.why: \(\frac{dA}{dt} = 2\pi r \times \frac{dr}{dt}\), so \(\frac{dA}{dt} = 2\pi \times 10 \times 3 = 60\pi \text{ m}^{2}/\text{min}\). The option \(30\pi\) comes from forgetting the 2 in \(2\pi r\).
a.clue: Differentiate \(A = \pi r^{2}\) with respect to \(t\) first.

b.q: Air fills a spherical balloon at \(36\pi \text{ cm}^{3}/\text{s}\). Using \(V = \frac{4}{3} \pi r^{3}\), how fast is the radius growing when \(r = 3\) cm?
b.why: \(\frac{dV}{dt} = 4\pi r^{2} \times \frac{dr}{dt}\), so \(36\pi = 4\pi \times 9 \times \frac{dr}{dt} = 36\pi \times \frac{dr}{dt}\). Then \(\frac{dr}{dt} = 1\) cm/s. The option 3 comes from dividing by \(12\pi\), which is wrong.
b.clue: Find \(\frac{dV}{dt}\) in terms of \(\frac{dr}{dt}\), then substitute \(r = 3\).
